newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 93 0 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 127 on last week

AMLC COMMENTARY: There was positive news for producers in beef markets this week starting with solid price gains for most categories of livestock. In North Asia, the favourable developments centred around the announcement of a South Korean tender and a sizeable depreciation in the value of the A$ against the Japanese yen.

The other piece of good news concerned a firming in the value of manufacturing beef on the U.S. market. This follows a period of sustained decline since March. A thorough drenching from the rain forecast for parts of Australia this weekend would cap the week off nicely.

Throughout the states, larger numbers of grain finished young cattle were presented at saleyards. These sold well, which helped boost young cattle price averages in most sales by 1-2c/kg lw. The grassfed offering struggled at times, but sold at rates similar to last week.

As noted in last week's report, with livestock prices increasing at the same time that export and wholesale prices remain flat, there has been a marked tightening in processor margins over the past month. To sustain current livestock price levels, export and wholesale prices will need to improve soon.
Developments in North Asia this week, although not bringing immediate export price relief, have been encouraging. The good news began with the announcement of a Korean tender, bidding date May 20.

In Japan, although trading remains quiet, export offer prices for Australian product were quoted firm to slightly higher. An important influence in the Japanese market this week has been the strengthening of the yen.

Since early may, a number of rumours concerning Japanese government moves on the yen have swept financial markets around the world. This marked a change in sentiment surrounding the Japanese currency and, over the past fortnight, the yen has firmed around nine percent against the A$.
In the U.S. beef prices improved by around 1USc/lb, which equated to a 2-4 Ac/kg increase to Australian exporters, partly on the back of buying for the Memorial Day Holiday (May 26).
